note: USACE Nashville District campground on the Fishing Creek arm of Lake Cumberland, west of Somerset. Wooded; the shore-row sites (04-13) sit 3-4 m above the summer lake at the top of a steep bank. Steep inclines between areas and a sharp entrance. Playground, boat ramp and day-use picnic area. --Claude
summary: Kept. Fees $30 confirmed (double site 03 $56, tent-only $24 noted). 46 sites (26 RV), 50A water/electric, max 66 ft; facilities + flush/potable; season 05-13..10-17 (was approximate Apr-Oct); weekend 2-night minimum, max 14. flags: WATERFRONT DOWNGRADE RECOMMENDED (stored lakefront -> lakeview): the shore-row RV sites 04 (37.0714,-84.6874), 06, 07, 09, 10, 11 and 13 are 9-12 m from Lake Cumberland's summer-pool line (723 ft = ~220.4 m), but USGS 3DEP 1-m lidar puts their pads at 223.4-225.9 m: 3.0-4.0 m (13: 5.5 m) above the summer edge, and the drop is a steep bank right off the pad (site 04: 224.3 m to 221.4 m within 3 m; 10: 223.3 to 220.8 within 3 m; 11: 222.8 to 219.3 within 3 m). The sites further east (15, 16, 19, 20, 24, 26) are 6-7 m above pool at 15-24 m. That is the curation doc's bluff/bench case (a 2-3.7 m bank at ~30 deg is a view): no RV site passes the kayak test. rec.gov's own text agrees: 'The campground is situated above the shore of Fishing Creek'. The view holds: on (leaf-off) Esri imagery the shore row looks over the water through a thin fringe of shoreline trees. The stored evidence ('pad row directly along Fishing Creek arm shoreline, nearest pads ~15-30m from waterline') measured distance only, not height.
